title.en: Anatomical side labelling and handedness of imported structures

summary: Verify that side labels come from the subject frame and that no structure is silently mirrored.
objective: Side labels stay correct from every camera position and every world matrix has the expected handedness.
applies_when: A model distinguishes left and right structures or laterality.
Geometry or volumes are imported from clinical or scanned data with their own coordinate convention.
Any transform in the chain may include a negative scale or a mirror.
intent_signals: is that the left ventricle or just screen left
example_prompts: Check the left and right labelling of this heart model from every angle.

principles: Anatomical left and right belong to the subject, not to the screen; a side label must be derived from the subject frame and stay correct as the camera moves.
A mirrored import is a handedness change: a world matrix with negative determinant swaps sides while still looking plausible.
Reference conventions are explicit data, so the mapping from the source coordinate convention to the scene axes is written down rather than judged by eye.
implementation: Write down the scene axes, the subject axes (anterior, superior, subject-left) and the exact mapping between them, including any intentional mirror.
Compute the determinant of the full world matrix of every imported structure and record its sign.
Place a landmark known to differ between sides and read its label from four camera positions, including directly behind the subject.
Inspect derived text as well: side labels, laterality filters and measurement panels often read from screen space instead of subject space.
observable_checks: Every structure world matrix has positive determinant unless a mirror is declared for that structure; a negative determinant together with a side label is a failure, and a zero determinant is a collapsed transform reported as its own case.
The asymmetric landmark keeps its side label from all four camera positions, including from behind, where screen-space labelling flips.
The written convention mapping reproduces the landmark position; an unwritten mapping counts as unverified rather than as passing.

known_limits: Checks orientation bookkeeping only; it does not verify anatomical accuracy, segmentation quality or fitness for any clinical use.
Authored verification guidance; no scene was run or rendered for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.

claims.statement: In the DICOM patient-based coordinate system the x axis increases toward the left hand side of the patient, the y axis toward the posterior side and the z axis toward the head.
claims.scope: DICOM patient-based coordinate system for biped patients; scene axes and rendering conventions are separate and must be mapped explicitly.
